Prevention: Sow early with the first rains
Remove volounteer plants from last crop
If field was infected previously, destroy plant debris under after harvest and rotate with cereal crops for 2 seasons
Consider using a fungicidal seed dressing as the disease is seedborne (see yellow direct control)
Monitoring: Inspect the field at least twice a week from crop emergence
Observe the undersides of the leaves for orange spots or reddish brown spores (these are the rust pustules)
Rust may occur at the same time as leafspot but unlike leaf spot, it does not cause defoliation
Start control measures immediatley after seeing the signs regardless of the severity
Direct Control (Non-chemical): There are no direct control methods
Restrictions: Use personal protective equipment when handling and applying pesticides, follow the label recommendations.
Do not eat, drink, smoke when mixing or applying pesticides.
In the field: spray chlorothalonil at intervals of 10-14 days and continue until 14 days before harvest.
Dilute 3ml of chlorothalonil in 1L of water.
WHO U (unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use)
PHI is 14 days.; REI is 12 hours; Do not apply direct to water or to areas where surface water is present as it is harzadous to acquatic life and wildlife
